options.content:
CPU and memory use of each container; one series per container. The synthetic data runs 120 minutes with 200 series per metric. | column | what it is | values | |---|---|---| | time | Time of the sample | One sample every 500 ms (2 per second) per series | | dimension | Always used: the queries read used CPU and memory | used | | container | Container name, in four groups: steady (no change), surge (CPU rises), leak (memory grows), idle (low CPU that later rises) | 200 values: steady-0 to steady-119 (120), surge-0 to surge-39 (40), leak-0 to leak-19 (20), idle-0 to idle-19 (20) | | container_cpu | CPU used, in cores | Usual values: normal distribution (mean 0.45, standard deviation 0.08) on container steady-0 to steady-119, container surge-0 to surge-39 and container leak-0 to leak-19; normal distribution (mean 0.15, standard deviation 0.03) on container idle-0 to idle-19
Minutes 30 to 80, ramping in and out over 15 minutes, each series starting 30 s after the previous one: values multiplied by 1.7 on container surge-0 to surge-39
Minutes 50 to 100, ramping in and out over 10 minutes, each series starting 30 s after the previous one: values multiplied by 2.2 on container idle-0 to idle-19
Note: never below 0 | | container_memory | Memory used, in bytes | Usual values: normal distribution (mean 900,000,000, standard deviation 80,000,000) on container steady-0 to steady-119, container surge-0 to surge-39 and container leak-0 to leak-19; normal distribution (mean 350,000,000, standard deviation 30,000,000) on container idle-0 to idle-19
Minutes 40 to the end, ramping in and out over 60 minutes, each series starting 60 s after the previous one: values multiplied by 1.8 on container leak-0 to leak-19
Note: never below 0 |

Each query runs twice, once with the exact plan and once with the approximate plan. A rule reads query results and decides an action; exact and approx decide separately, and the dashboard compares their decisions. On the time charts below, shaded areas are the problem periods injected into the synthetic data.

**Queries**

| query | PromQL | computed |
|---|---|---|
| p95_cpu | `quantile_over_time(0.95, container_cpu{dimension="used"}[5m])` | every 60 s over the last 300 s |
| p95_memory | `quantile_over_time(0.95, container_memory{dimension="used"}[5m])` | every 60 s over the last 300 s |
| p50_cpu_1h | `quantile_over_time(0.5, container_cpu{dimension="used"}[1h])` | every 60 s over the last 3,600 s |
| p95_cpu_1h | `quantile_over_time(0.95, container_cpu{dimension="used"}[1h])` | every 60 s over the last 3,600 s |
| p99_memory_1h | `quantile_over_time(0.99, container_memory{dimension="used"}[1h])` | every 60 s over the last 3,600 s |
| max_memory_1h | `max_over_time(container_memory{dimension="used"}[1h])` | every 60 s over the last 3,600 s |

**Rules**

| rule | queries it uses | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| scale_decision | p95_cpu, p95_memory | Scale a container up when its p95 CPU > 0.8 cores or p95 memory > 1.5 GB; scale it down when p95 CPU < 0.4 cores and p95 memory < 0.75 GB |
| ec2_scale_out | p95_cpu | p95 CPU over 5 minutes at or above 60% of one core for 3 periods in a row: the step alarm that adds capacity (AWS EC2 Auto Scaling; 3 periods ours) |
| ec2_scale_in | p95_cpu | p95 CPU over 5 minutes below 40% of one core for 3 periods in a row: the step alarm that removes capacity (AWS EC2 Auto Scaling; 3 periods ours) |
| vpa | p50_cpu_1h, p95_cpu_1h, max_memory_1h | The CPU request of 0.6 cores falls outside [p50, p95] × 1.15 of the last hour, or the memory peak × 1.15 exceeds the 1.6 GB request: the updater resizes the pod (Kubernetes Vertical Pod Autoscaler; 1 hour instead of 8 days; requests ours) |
| grafana_labs | p95_cpu_1h | p95 CPU of the last hour above the 0.6-core request: under-provisioned (Grafana Labs; 1 hour instead of 7 days; request ours) |
| azure_advisor | p95_cpu_1h, p99_memory_1h | On half the size (0.5 cores, 1 GB), p95 CPU of the last hour stays at most 40% and p99 memory at most 60%: recommend the smaller size (Azure Advisor, user-facing; 1 hour instead of 7 days; sizes ours) |

panels.title: Every run and query: plan, query error, and what the application saw
panels.description: Each row is one query in one run, paired with one rule or alert that reads it; a query read by three rules has three rows. Sketch and parameters are the approximate plan the planner chose: the sketch type and its size (for KMV, k is how many hashes it keeps; for HLL, precision p means 2^p registers). Fidelity compares the rule's decisions on the exact and approx answers: an episode is a stretch of consecutive evaluations where the exact rule fires, an incident is an attack or change the data generator injected (synthetic data only). Hover a fidelity cell to read all of it.

Rollout controller: rollouts decided the same. Top clients: mean clients shared by the exact and approx top lists, as a fraction of the list size. Rule: entity-evaluations where exact and approx agree on whether the rule is active.
